name: carousel
description: Horizontally scrolling slide strip built on CSS scroll-snap, progressively enhanced with prev/next buttons, dot indicators and a polite live region

viewport.description: The scroll-snap strip itself: an inline-axis scroll container holding the slides. Focusable (tabindex="0") so it is keyboard-scrollable with no JavaScript

slide.description: One snap target; repeated per slide. Carries role="group" + aria-roledescription="slide" and a positional aria-label

controls.description: Wrapper for the prev/next buttons. Ships `hidden` — inert without the controller, which un-hides it on init

prev.description: Scrolls to the previous slide; disabled on the first slide unless the root carries data-loop

next.description: Scrolls to the next slide; disabled on the last slide unless the root carries data-loop

dots.description: Wrapper for the dot indicators. Ships `hidden` alongside the controls

dot.description: Reflects the current slide (data-state="active" + aria-current="true") and jumps to its slide when activated; one per slide

status.description: Polite live region (role="status") the controller updates with "Slide N of M" on every slide change

active.description: The dot for the current slide; paired with aria-current="true"

loop.description: Boundary contract. Absent (default) = stop: the controller disables prev on the first slide and next on the last. Present = loop: next past the last wraps to the first and prev past the first wraps to the last, and neither button is ever disabled

slideSize.description: Flex basis of each slide, so a strip can show more than one slide at a time (e.g. 60% for a peeking layout). Purely CSS — the controller measures whatever the layout produces

required_attrs: aria-label (or aria-labelledby) naming the carousel on root
aria-label on slide giving its position ("2 of 5")
tabindex="0" on viewport so the scroll region is keyboard-reachable

keyboard.Tab: moves through the viewport, then the prev/next buttons, then the dots
keyboard.ArrowLeft/ArrowRight: native scrolling of the focused viewport — the browser scrolls and scroll-snap settles on the neighbouring slide (no JavaScript involved)
keyboard.Home/End: native scroll of the focused viewport to the first/last slide
keyboard.Enter/Space: activates the focused prev/next button or dot

a11y.notes: Progressive enhancement is the whole design. CSS scroll-snap slides the strip, so with JavaScript disabled the component is a complete, keyboard-operable scroller; the controls and dots — which do nothing without a controller — ship `hidden` and are un-hidden on init (and re-hidden by destroy()). Slides are never aria-hidden: they stay in the scroll container and in the accessibility tree, which is what lets assistive tech and find-in-page reach off-screen content. The [data-part='status'] live region announces "Slide N of M" politely on each change. Reduced motion is honoured with an explicit behavior: "instant" scroll (which overrides the CSS scroll-behavior: smooth) plus a scroll-behavior: auto override in the media query for native scrolls. No autoplay: an unattended moving carousel would need pause/stop controls to meet WCAG 2.2.2, and none of that JavaScript is worth the budget.

templates.html:
{slide1}
{slide2}

api.goTo: (index) => void — scroll to a slide, wrapped or clamped per the loop-or-stop contract
api.next: () => void — scroll to the next slide
api.prev: () => void — scroll to the previous slide
api.destroy: () => void — remove the click/scroll listeners, re-hide the enhancement-only controls, and drop the private handle

faqir:change.description: Fires whenever the current slide changes — from a button, a dot, or the reader scrolling/swiping the strip themselves (scroll math, rAF-throttled). Does not fire for a navigation that lands on the slide already showing.

js_budget.note: The controller is buttons + dots + a live region only — the sliding is CSS. Budget is 1.5 KB gzip of the minified file (bun build --minify | gzip), the same measurement scripts/check-size.mjs applies to the bundles; pinned by tests/recipes/carousel.test.ts.
